title: A bill to permit States to transfer certain funds from the clean water revolving fund of a State to the drinking water revolving fund of the State in certain circumstances, and for other purposes.
official_summary: This bill allows—for one year—a state to transfer amounts from its clean water state revolving fund to its drinking water state revolving fund in order to address a threat to public health as a result of heightened exposure to lead in drinking water. Specifically, a state may transfer no more than 5% of the cumulative amount of the federal grant dollars awarded for its clean water state revolving fund to its drinking water state revolving fund.

summary.headline: A one-year law lets states move some clean water loan funds into drinking water loan funds to address lead exposure threats.
summary.what_it_does: For one year, a state may shift up to 5% of the total federal grant money it has received for its clean water state revolving fund into its drinking water state revolving fund. The transfer is allowed only to address a public health threat from heightened lead exposure in drinking water. The title also says the bill includes other provisions, but the official summary describes only this transfer authority.

who_it_affects.group: State governments that run clean water and drinking water state revolving funds
who_it_affects.how: They gain temporary authority to move up to 5% of their clean water fund's cumulative federal grant amount into their drinking water fund to respond to lead risks.

who_it_affects.group: Residents served by public drinking water systems in areas with lead exposure concerns
who_it_affects.how: Their state may use the transferred money to help fund drinking water work aimed at reducing lead exposure.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted October 4, 2019; the transfer authority lasts for one year.
